v4.description: Look back at the user's own saved original messages from before today. This is a read-only lookup: it changes nothing and is NOT for correcting, forgetting or changing remembered information (those are separate actions). Do not use it for today's conversation, or for a greeting, small talk, a new subject or an unrelated remark. When you call it, call it alone, without any reply text; the answer is written after the lookup finishes. Resolve dates yourself from the time context into YYYY-MM-DD in the user's timezone. Two ways to ask. (1) By date: when the user names or points to a past calendar date or period (up to about three months), for example 'what did I tell you on August 20', 'what did we talk about yesterday', 'go over last week', or 'when did I first mention painting' (use a wide range from the far past), give start_date (and end_date for a run of dates). Also use it, with time_basis experienced_date, when they ask what HAPPENED or what they DID on a past day ('what did I do yesterday'). A follow-up asking for a detail of a period you already recapped should call it again for that period so the answer comes from the original words, not from your earlier summary. (2) By search: when the user asks about an ordinary thing, experience or person they told you about some time ago (weeks or months back) without a date you can resolve, for example 'did I ever tell you about playing the piano?', give search_terms: 2 to 5 short keywords or phrases exactly as they would literally appear in the user's own messages, including close synonyms and, when the user mixes languages, the forms in each language. Optionally add people (names or relationship words as the user would have written them) and a start_date/end_date range if the user gave a period. (3) By continuation: when the user does NOT ask about the past but their current message only makes sense with something they told you earlier (a pronoun or omission such as 'they finally wrote back', 'she called again', 'it went better this time') and the current message, the user's last few messages or the DialogueState topic give enough clues to say what the earlier thing was likely about, search with search_terms taken from those clues (never from your own earlier replies) and set continuation_basis to the signals you used: current_input, adjacent_user (the user's recent messages) and/or dialogue_state (only if a DialogueState section is present). Use continuation also when the person tells you how they feel about something specific (a person, project, decision or plan) and what the person told you before matters to understanding what they actually care about here: take search_terms from words that literally appear in the current message (a name, a project, the thing itself) and set continuation_basis to current_input. The result is background; it is used only if it bears on what they just said. Never search merely because another topic is related, and never to bring up an unrelated trip or event to show you remember. Do not use it when the earlier context is already in the conversation, when nothing in the current talk points to an earlier matter, or just to be thorough. Search terms are only clues for finding the messages; they are not facts about the user.
